question: Example: what are the mass-ratio and fill-out distributions of a homogeneous sample of totally eclipsing contact binaries without published light-curve solutions?

audience.who: Observers and modellers of W UMa-type contact binaries.

citations.citation: Example A et al. Photometric solutions of contact binaries.
Example B et al. Low-mass-ratio contact binaries from TESS.

closest_prior_work.what_it_shows: Solutions for a different sample of nine systems.
closest_prior_work.our_difference: A homogeneous, larger sample with one pipeline, MCMC uncertainties and a Gaia luminosity check.

decisive_analysis.description: Light-curve solutions of the sample with posterior uncertainties.

feasibility_precheck.description: Reproduce the published solution (q, i, fill-out) of one comparable totally eclipsing system from the same public TESS light curve with the line's pipeline.
feasibility_precheck.pass_criterion: q, i and fill-out each within the published 1-sigma uncertainties (or within 2 sigma of the combined uncertainty)

primary_endpoint.metric: posterior median q and fill-out per target with 68% intervals
primary_endpoint.split: targets with published solutions held out as a check
primary_endpoint.decision_rule: sample statistics reported only if all held-out checks agree within 2 sigma
primary_endpoint.stop_rule: stop if more than one held-out check disagrees

data_sources.version: TESS sectors as retrieved (record in receipt)
data_sources.license: public archive data; cite per MAST acknowledgement

computational_only_rationale: Re-analysis of public survey photometry; no observing time or real-world interaction.

cost_estimate.basis: Example: per-target solve measured in the line's validation baseline.
